summary: San Jose sprawls across 181 square miles of the Santa Clara Valley floor — nearly the land area of three San Franciscos — yet most of that flatness is ringed by the Diablo Range to the east and the Santa Cruz Mountains to the west, which means winter sunsets drop behind forested ridgelines visible from ordinary parking lots. That geographic bowl helps explain why the city averages 9.6 hours of daily sunshine and an annual high around 71°F: warm enough for year-round cycling on the Guadalupe River Trail or hiking in Alum Rock Park, cool enough at a 51°F average low that summer nights rarely need air conditioning. As the self-proclaimed "Capital of Silicon Valley," San Jose is genuinely a job center — Adobe, Cisco, and PayPal all headquarter here — so the median household income hits $141,565, yet the median home still lists at nearly $1.19 million, producing a price-to-income ratio above 8:1, roughly double the national norm. Rent at $2,617 per month absorbs a smaller but still substantial share. The city's motor-vehicle-theft rate of 609 per 100K is notably elevated, a practical consideration for anyone parking on the street. At its core, San Jose is a place where high-paying employment and mild weather coexist with a housing cost structure that turns even strong incomes into careful monthly arithmetic.
